62 bends and 601 torsions the 2024 file lacks for united-atom hydrocarbons, alcohols and ethers, from Jorgensen, Madura & Swenson, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 106, 6638 (1984), Tables I and II; Jorgensen, J. Phys. Chem. 90, 1276 (1986), Tables II and III; Briggs, Matsui & Jorgensen, J. Comput. Chem. 11, 958 (1990), Table II and p. 960 (bench/ff/open/oplsua2024_supplement.json; each term's comment names its table and anything taken from the 2024 file); the 2024 file's own terms win

the papers' torsions were fit with fixed bond lengths and angles, no 1-4 Lennard-Jones and weak terms beyond 1-4 (1984 eq 3: C-C sigma 4 A, epsilon 0.0074; 1986: HO-CH3 sigma 2.6 A, epsilon 0.008; 1990 eq 3: sigma 2.745 A, epsilon 0.008 kcal/mol); here they run with the 2024 file's flexible bonds and its 1-4 x 0.5 scaling

none of the three papers has a torsion about a C-C bond between two oxygens (O-C-C-O: poly(ethylene oxide), glycols) or an O-C-O acetal term; those are CAPS's fits to RI-MP2/cc-pVTZ//HF/6-31G** relaxed scans of all-atom fragments (1,2-dimethoxyethane, 2-methoxyethanol, acetal and glycidyl-ether fragments) with the united-atom model evaluated on them (caps.torsionfit), each comment giving its RMS; hydroxyl torsions whose scans are dominated by an intramolecular OH...O hydrogen bond (RMS over 1.1 kcal/mol) are not fitted and stay missing
